title: fix(core): a date-only value renders the calendar day it names, in every timezone (objectui#10110)
body:
Part of #10110 — the display half that lives in `packages/core/src/utils/`, which is this seat's ruled file surface. See "What this PR leaves open" for the rest of that card.

## What was wrong

ECMAScript parses the two ISO shapes in two different zones: a DATE-ONLY form is UTC, a date-time form without an offset is local. `date-display.ts` parsed every string value with one `new Date(value)`, so `2026-08-01` became UTC midnight and was then read back through this module's LOCAL getters — `getFullYear` / `getMonth` / `getDate`, and `toLocaleDateString`'s own. West of UTC that lands on the previous calendar day, which is what the card measured: a stored `2026-08-01` rendered `7月31日` for a UTC-7 viewer while the API response and a UTC+8 viewer both said August 1st.

The relative branch shifted with it, one day per day, because it compares two LOCAL start-of-days: `2026-08-31` read `4天前` on the 3rd. One root cause, two visible faces.

## The repair

One parse step, `toDisplayDate`, that every function in the module now goes through. A date-only value names a calendar day and carries no instant, so there is nothing to convert: it is rebuilt at LOCAL midnight of the day it names, and every getter downstream reports that day in every zone.

⛔ No hours are added or subtracted anywhere. An offset that cancelled the shift would be wrong again at a DST boundary and wrong in the other direction east of UTC, where the old parse already landed on the right day — see the ablation matrix below, where exactly that fake repair is measured.

Three properties held on purpose:

- **A value carrying a time is untouched.** It HAS an instant and rendering an instant in the viewer's zone is what `datetime` is for. The split is the VALUE's spelling, never a declared field type, which this pure module cannot see: `2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z` still reads `Jul 31` in the west.
- **Acceptance is unchanged.** The engine's own parse still decides what is a date at all, and only a value it already accepted is rebuilt — `2026-13-01` is still the em dash, and a well-shaped impossible day still ROLLS (`2026-02-30` renders March 2nd), which is the behaviour `dataset-format.ts`'s date suite pins.
- **No API moved.** No new export, no new option, no signature change — `Clause-②: no` holds. `@object-ui/fields` re-exports the same four names.

Callers that hand these functions the wire string move with the repair: the `date` cell and its readonly field face, `ObjectGrid` date columns and mobile cards, `ObjectGantt` tooltips, `FormulaField`, lookup column display, and dataset date measures.

## Pinned across four real timezones, not one

⭐ The suite pins `TZ=UTC` (objectui#8366), which is the single offset at which this defect is invisible — presumably how it shipped. So `date-display.dateOnlyZone-10110.test.ts` drives the zone as an INPUT, two zones west of UTC and two east, plus instant controls that must NOT move.

⚠️ One mechanism finding worth carrying: **writing `process.env.TZ` inside a test does not move the zone here, and it fails silently.** The root config runs `pool: 'threads'`, so a test body runs in a worker thread where `process.env` is a plain copy with no native setter behind it — the assignment lands, `Intl` still reports `UTC`, and every date-only assertion passes for the wrong reason. The first draft of this pin had that shape and went green against the UNFIXED code. Each zone is therefore read from a real child process started with `TZ` in its environment, with the clock frozen the same way; the first case asserts the child reports the zone it was given, so a rig that stops working reds instead of going quiet.

Zones driven: `America/Los_Angeles` (the card's machine, UTC-7), `America/Santiago` (UTC-4/-3, and `2026-09-06` has no local midnight there), `Asia/Shanghai` (UTC+8), `Pacific/Kiritimati` (UTC+14).

## Verification

| run | result |
| --- | --- |
| `vitest run packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/date-display.dateOnlyZone-10110.test.ts` | 17 passed |
| 25 date-family files across `core` / `components` / `fields` / `plugin-grid` / `plugin-gantt` / `plugin-dashboard` | 438 passed, 0 failed |
| `tsc --noEmit` + `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` for `@object-ui/core`, after building its dependency closure | exit 0, no diagnostics (the first attempt reported TS6305 only because the closure was not built yet) |
| `vitest run packages/core/` | 160 files, 3367 passed |
| `check:control-bytes` · `check:test-path-roots` · `check:changeset-claims` · `check:pending-changeset-literals` · `check:new-line-citations` · `check:unreferenced-sources` · `check:vi-mock-specifiers` · changeset presence | all exit 0 |
| `eslint --no-inline-config` on the two changed source files | exit 0, 2 files, 0 errors (1 pre-existing-style `no-explicit-any` warning on the one surviving cast) |

`check:changeset-claims` reports one pending changeset naming this file — the objectui#7178 move declaration, whose claim is that the MOVE changed no behaviour. Re-read: still true of that change; the behaviour change here is declared by this PR's own changeset.

### Ablation, run against the committed repair

Each leg: mutate, prove the mutation reached disk (anchor count both directions plus a blob-hash change), run the pin, restore from `HEAD`, prove `git diff HEAD` empty.

- **A — revert `toDisplayDate` to the plain parse:** 9 failed / 8 passed. Every date-only face reds; the instant controls, the east-of-UTC absolute case and the rig check stay green.
- **B — the fake repair, twelve hours added to the parsed instant instead:** 2 failed / 15 passed. ⭐ Every case the card reported, west of UTC, stays GREEN. The only reds are `Pacific/Kiritimati` and the all-zones-agree case. A pin driven in the reported zone alone would have signed this off — which is the argument for driving both directions.
- **C — drop the `setFullYear` line:** 1 failed / 16 passed, the two-digit-year case alone (years 0-99 map onto 1900+y through the multi-argument constructor, which the string parse does not do).

The full measured matrix is in the test file's header, with the two predictions it falsified.

## What this PR leaves open

⛔ Three display sites outside `packages/core/src/utils/` parse a date-only value themselves and are NOT reached by this repair. They are reported to the PM seat for filing rather than repaired here, because the file surface for this card is one directory:

1. `packages/components/src/renderers/complex/data-table.tsx` — the cell formatter pre-parses with `Date.parse` and hands `formatDate` a `Date`, so the value arrives already shifted and the shared repair cannot see it. Its own convention pin runs in UTC and cannot see it either.
2. `packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailView.tsx` — the summary chip's `date` branch parses and formats on its own.
3. `packages/app-shell/src/utils/auditHistoryDisplay.ts` — the audit / history value formatter's `date` branch, same shape.

All three shift the same way in `America/Los_Angeles` for the same input. The card's own measured surfaces — the list cell, the related-list grid and the record-detail field, absolute and relative — are covered by this PR, so this PR says `Part of` and carries no closing keyword: whether objectui#10110 is done here, or waits for those three, is the maintainer's call and not this PR's to make silently.

## Acceptance notes

- noted, not filed: `packages/fields/src/index.tsx`'s `DateCellRenderer` sets its `title` from the parsed instant (`toISOString`) and feeds the same instant to its overdue test, so for a date-only value the tooltip shows a UTC instant the cell no longer displays. Cosmetic, one package over, and `packages/fields/` is held by an unmerged card — carrier: whoever lands next in that file.
- noted, not filed: `packages/plugin-detail/src/InlineFieldInput.tsx` converts a date input back through `new Date(v + 'T00:00:00')` on WRITE. Not touched here: the card rules the stored value correct and the write path out of scope.
